_doc: SHIFTZOOM: the Shift-constrained Rect drag run OFF the identity view —
the square twin of draw_ellipse_shift_zoomed.json, same view and same
drag, so the two vectors differ only in the tool.
draw_rect_shift.json runs at zoom 1.0, where the screen->document
conversion (`doc = (screen - view_offset) / zoom`) hands the tool exact
integers, so every doc-space anchor is dyadic and the arithmetic below is
exact by luck. That is why the original SHIFTCONSTRAIN smoke test — run
by hand at 100% zoom — saw a true square.
At zoom 1.5 the anchor is NOT dyadic. Geometry, by hand, from
`doc = screen / 1.5` (offset 0):
press   screen ( 30,  50) -> doc ( 20, 100/3)
release screen (120,  95) -> doc ( 80, 190/3)
ddx = 80 - 20       = 60     (the furthest reach)
side = max(|ddx|, |ddy|) = 60     -> width = height = 60
The drag is down-and-right, so the square grows into that quadrant from
the press point and the top-left corner stays the anchor: x = 20,
y = 100/3 = 33.3333 (4 dp, the canonical rounding).
WHY THIS VECTOR NEEDS `expected_exact`. The canonical document JSON
rounds every float to 4 decimal places, so it CANNOT see the defect this
case exists for: before the fix the commit recovered the side as
`abs(doc_end_y - doc_start_y)`, re-subtracting the anchor that had just
been added to it, and 100/3 + 60 - 100/3 comes back one ulp heavy (the
sum crosses the 64 binade). width was 60.0 and height 60.00000000000001 —
not a square — and the 4-dp golden below reads 60.0 either way. The
`expected_exact` block is the real gate: it compares the committed
doubles at FULL precision, exactly as `expected_view` does for the view
triple.
`rx`/`ry` in the golden are the rect's CORNER radii (both 0), not the
size — the size fields to pin here are width and height.
name: draw_rect_shift_zoomed_is_a_square_at_non_dyadic_zoom
